article.Citation/Title: Yoon, G., Petrakis, I. L., & Krystal, J. H. (2019). Association of combined naltrexone and ketamine with depressive symptoms in a case series of patients with depression and alcohol use disorder. JAMA Psychiatry, 76(3), 337-338.
article.Outcome: 100% (5 of 5) met clinical response criteria (≥50% MADRS improvement) by their fourth ketamine infusion
article.InterventionDescription: Naltrexone 380 mg IM once, 2-6 days before first ketamine dose; ketamine 0.5 mg/kg IV weekly x4 infusions over 4 weeks; 8-week open-label VA pilot.

article.Outcome: Methods states the primary outcome measure is clinical response (≥50% MADRS improvement from baseline at 4 hours postinfusion). Results reports two time points for this measure: 60% (3/5) responded after the initial dose and 100% (5/5) responded by the fourth dose. The cumulative, endpoint figure (100%, 5/5) was chosen as the primary-comparison value since it represents the study's full-course result on the designated primary outcome; the earlier 60% figure is the interim assessment after dose 1.
article.SD: No dispersion measure, test statistic, or df is reported anywhere in the article for the MADRS response-rate outcome; this is a research letter reporting only raw counts/percentages, so SD is coded not reported.
article.PVal: No p-value is reported for the clinical-response outcome (or for any outcome in the article); coded not reported.
article.SampleSize_NFinal: The 100% (5 of 5) response-by-fourth-dose figure explicitly states N=5 as its denominator (Results paragraph), so SampleSize_NFinal=5. Note an apparent internal tension: the same sentence also states '1 patient left the trial after receiving 2 ketamine infusions,' which is not decoded or reconciled here per the never-construct-a-decoding-theory rule — the article's own stated denominator (5 of 5) is reported as printed rather than inferred down to 4.

MethodologyDescribedYN.note: Brief research-letter format. sample_size_power=N: no sample-size justification or power calculation is discussed anywhere. statistical_methods=N: results are reported as raw percentages/counts with no statistical-testing methodology described. comparator=Y and randomization=Y are coded as 'described as absent': the title and Methods explicitly frame the design as a 'case series' and 'open-label pilot study,' which is an explicit (if terse) statement that no control/comparator arm and no randomization were used, satisfying the described-as-absent standard rather than mere silence. n_met=12 < 13, so MethodologyDescribedYN=0.

config_proposal.note: Single-arm, no-comparator case series (N=5); the primary outcome is a pre/post response-rate proportion with no dispersion, test statistic, or comparison group, so none of the seven supported conversion methods (d, g, eta_p, F, chi2, OR, RR) apply. Excluded from Tier 1, routed to Tier 2.
config_proposal.tier2_basis: 100% (5/5) met the pre-specified clinical response criterion by the fourth ketamine infusion, and 80% (4/5) reported improved alcohol craving/consumption on the OCDS, in a single-arm open-label design with no comparator.
